paper.title_en: Correlations between $\ensuremath{\mitΥ(n\text{S})}\xspace$ production and the underlying event in $\ensuremath{p\!p}\xspace$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
paper.abstract_en: Recent studies from various experiments at the LHC and RHIC suggest that small collision systems exhibit quark-gluon plasma (QGP) like signatures that were typically observed in large systems. While QGP like signatures have been observed in the soft sector, strong constraints on possible partonic energy loss were established in the hard sector. At the same time, there are multiple pieces of evidence pointing to correlations between hard and soft particle production in proton-proton collisions. The correlations between hard and soft particle production in $pp$ collisions are studied in events with $Υ$ mesons, which provide a valuable hard probe to study such effects. The multiplicity and distributions of kinematic variables of charged particles produced in association with an $Υ$ meson are measured using 139 fb$^{-1}$ of data at $\ensuremath{\sqrt{s}}\xspace = 13$~TeV collected by the ATLAS experiment at the LHC. The measurement is performed separately for the first three $Υ$(nS) states in intervals of their transverse momentum. At low transverse momentum, the associated charged-particle multiplicity is observed to be systematically lower in collisions where $Υ$(2S) or $Υ$(3S) is produced compared to $Υ$(1S), with the difference decreasing as the $Υ$ transverse momentum increases.
